6613-myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-v.title: Our Own Land
6613-myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-v.creator: Charles M. Skinner
6613-myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-v.description: A book by Charles M. Skinner. Mount Tacoma has always been a place of superstitious regard among the Siwash (Sauvage) of the Northwest. In their myths it was the place of refuge for the last man when the Whulge was so swollen after long rain that its waters covered the earth. All other men were drowned. The waves pursued the one man as he climbed, rising higher and higher until they came to his knees, his waist, his breast.

arxiv-2103-00573.title: RuSentEval: Linguistic Source, Encoder Force!
arxiv-2103-00573.creator: Vladislav Mikhailov, Ekaterina Taktasheva, Elina Sigdel, Ekaterina Artemova
arxiv-2103-00573.description: Abstract The success of pre-trained transformer language models has brought a great deal of interest on how these models work, and what they learn about language. However, prior research in the field is mainly devoted to English, and little is known regarding other languages.

arxiv-2104-11554.title: Sketch-based Normal Map Generation with Geometric Sampling
arxiv-2104-11554.creator: Yi He, Haoran Xie, Chao Zhang, Xi Yang, Kazunori Miyata
arxiv-2104-11554.description: Abstract Normal map is an important and efficient way to represent complex 3D models. A designer may benefit from the auto-generation of high quality and accurate normal maps from freehand sketches in 3D content creation. This paper proposes a deep generative model for generating normal maps from users’ sketch with geometric sampling.

arxiv-2112-03044.title: Fusion Detection via Distance-Decay IoU and weighted Dempster-Shafer Evidence Theory
arxiv-2112-03044.creator: Fang Qingyun and Wang Zhaokui
arxiv-2112-03044.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fang Qingyun and Wang Zhaokui. In recent years, increasing attentions are paid on object detection in remote sensing imagery. However, traditional optical detection is highly susceptible to illumination and weather anomaly. It is a challenge to effectively utilize the cross-modality information from multi-source remote sensing images, especially from optical and synthetic aperture radar images, to achieve all-day and all-weather detection with high accuracy and speed. Towards this end, a fast multi-source fusion detection framework is proposed in current paper.

arxiv-2201-12777.title: On the automorphism groups of Lunardon-Polverino scattered linear sets
arxiv-2201-12777.creator: Wei Tang 1, Yue Zhou 1, † \dagger, Ferdinando Zullo 2
arxiv-2201-12777.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Wei Tang 1, Yue Zhou 1, † \dagger, Ferdinando Zullo 2. Lunardon and Polverino introduced in 2001 a new family of maximum scattered linear sets in PG ⁡ ( 1 , q n ) \mathrm{PG}(1,q^{n}) to construct linear minimal Rédei blocking sets. This family has been extended first by Lavrauw, Marino, Trombetti and Polverino in 2015 and then by Sheekey in 2016 in two different contexts (semifields and rank metric codes).

arxiv-2310-10710.title: Bootstrapping string theory EFT
arxiv-2310-10710.creator: Li-Yuan Chiang, Yu-tin Huang, He-Chen Weng
arxiv-2310-10710.description: Abstract We study the space of open string effective field theories by combining the constraint of unitarity and monodromy relations for the four-point amplitude. The latter is a reflection of an underlying disk correlator with singularities at the boundary. By assuming maximal susy the resulting bootstrap isolates Wilson coefficients to at least 10 − 4 10^{-4} of the Type-I superstring.

arxiv-2311-14179.title: Philosophy of contraherent cosheaves
arxiv-2311-14179.creator: Leonid Positselski
arxiv-2311-14179.description: Abstract . Contraherent cosheaves are module objects over algebraic varieties defined by gluing using the colocalization functors. Contraherent cosheaves are designed to be used for globalizing contramodules and contraderived categories for the purposes of Koszul duality and semi-infinite algebraic geometry. One major technical problem associated with contraherent cosheaves is that the colocalization functors, unlike the localizations, are not exact.

arxiv-2401-00466.title: Online Symbolic Music Alignment with Offline Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2401-00466.description: Abstract Symbolic Music Alignment is the process of matching performed MIDI notes to corresponding score notes. In this paper, we introduce a reinforcement learning (RL)-based online symbolic music alignment technique. The RL agent — an attention-based neural network — iteratively estimates the current score position from local score and performance contexts.

arxiv-2402-09901.title: Analysis of B ( s ) 0 → μ + ​ μ − B^{0}_{(s)}\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-} decays at the LHC
arxiv-2402-09901.creator: Kai-Feng Chen *, Titus Mombächer *, Umberto de Sanctis *
arxiv-2402-09901.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kai-Feng Chen *, Titus Mombächer *, Umberto de Sanctis *. This article reviews the most recent measurements of B ( s ) 0 → μ + ​ μ − B_{(s)}^{0}\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-} decay properties at the LHC, which are the most precise to date.

arxiv-2403-03519.title: KIAS Lectures on Symplectic Aspects of Degenerations
arxiv-2403-03519.creator: Jonny Evans
arxiv-2403-03519.description: Abstract This is a series of three lectures I gave at the Korea Institute of Advanced Study in June 2019 at a workshop about “Algebraic and Symplectic Aspects of Degenerations of Complex Surfaces”. I will focus on the symplectic aspects, in particular on the case of cyclic quotient surface singularities.

arxiv-2408-14398.title: On the Limitations of Language Targeted Pruning: Investigating the Calibration Language Impact in Multilingual LLM Pruning
arxiv-2408-14398.creator: Simon Kurz, Jian-Jia Chen, Lucie Flek, Zhixue Zhao
arxiv-2408-14398.description: Abstract Recent advances in large language model (LLM) pruning have shown state-of-the-art (SotA) compression results in post-training and retraining-free settings while maintaining high predictive performance. However, previous research mainly considered calibrating based on English text, despite the multilingual nature of modern LLMs and their frequent use in non-English languages.

arxiv-2412-12977.title: Chirally motivated π ​ Σ − K ¯ ​ N \pi\Sigma-\bar{K}N model in a finite volume Journal: Eur. Phys. J. A
arxiv-2412-12977.creator: Peter C. Bruns e1, Aleš Cieplý e2
arxiv-2412-12977.description: Abstract We generalize the chirally motivated π ​ Σ − K ¯ ​ N \pi\Sigma-\bar{K}N coupled channels model to the cubic finite volume and use it to calculate the stationary energy spectrum that appears in a nice agreement with the spectrum obtained in the lattice QCD simulations by the BaSc collaboration.

arxiv-2507-21288.title: Learning Simulatable Models of Cloth with Spatially-varying Constitutive Properties
arxiv-2507-21288.creator: Guanxiong Chen, Shashwat Suri, Yuhao Wu, Etienne Voulga, David I.W. Levin, Dinesh K. Pai
arxiv-2507-21288.description: Abstract Materials used in real clothing exhibit remarkable complexity and spatial variation due to common processes such as stitching, hemming, dyeing, printing, padding, and bonding. Simulating these materials, for instance using finite element methods, is often computationally demanding and slow. Worse, such methods can suffer from numerical artifacts called “membrane locking” that makes cloth appear artificially stiff.

arxiv-2509-22377.title: Effectiveness of large multimodal models in detecting disinformation: experimental results
arxiv-2509-22377.creator: Yasmina Kheddache, Marc Lalonde
arxiv-2509-22377.description: Abstract The proliferation of disinformation, particularly in multimodal contexts combining text and images, presents a significant challenge across digital platforms. This study investigates the potential of large multimodal models (LMMs) in detecting and mitigating false information. We propose to approach multimodal disinformation detection by leveraging the advanced capabilities of the GPT-4o model.

arxiv-2602-12059.title: Evaluation of Security-Induced Latency on 5G RAN Interfaces and User Plane Communication Conference: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Conference on Security and Privacy in Wireless and Mobile Networks; June 30-July 03, 2026; Saarbrücken, Germany Proceedings of the 19th ACM Conference on Security and Priv

arxiv-2602-12059.description: Abstract . 5G promises enhanced performance—not only in bandwidth and capacity, but also latency and security. Its ultra-reliable low-latency configuration targets round-trip times below 1 ms, while optional security controls extend protection across all interfaces, making 5G attractive for mission-critical applications.

pmc-12652576.title: Differential Features of Cholecystokinin-Releasing Peptides Derived from Food Proteins: Peptide Length, Amino Acid Composition and Primary Structure; Analysis of Currently Identified Peptide Sequences
pmc-12652576.creator: Giovanni Tulipano, Giovanni Grazioso
pmc-12652576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The mouse enteroendocrine cell line STC-1 has been widely used to investigate the effects of dietary protein-derived peptides on cholecystokinin (CCK) secretion. The studies have also addressed the question of whether specific structural features of a given peptide chain may be related to higher secretagogue activity with respect to others, but a detailed structure–activity relationship in CCK-releasing peptides has not yet been reported.

pmc-12655450.title: Robust All-Solid-State Batteries with Sodium Ion Electrolyte, Aluminum and Additive Manufacturing Inconel 625 Electrodes
pmc-12655450.creator: Manuela C. Baptista, Antonio B. Vale, Jose M. Costa, Maria Helena Braga
pmc-12655450.description: This study investigates all-solid-state batteries employing multifunctional metallic current collectors/electrodes that remain electrochemically inert toward an alkali-based Na ion solid electrolyte. Inconel 625 was evaluated as the positive current collector in combination with aluminum as the negative electrode and the ferroelectric electrolyte Na2.99Ba0.005OCl.

pmc-13109033.title: Decreased Myocardial 123I‐MIBG Uptake Without Sympathetic Denervation: An Autopsy Report of Autoimmune Autonomic Ganglionopathy
pmc-13109033.creator: Daisuke Taniguchi, Kenya Nishioka, Yuta Ishiguro, Tsuyoshi Furuya, Takashi Ogawa, Kazunori Kajino, Yoshiaki Furukawa, Nobutaka Hattori
pmc-13109033.description: IntroductionAutoimmune autonomic ganglionopathy (AAG) is a rare disorder characterized by widespread autonomic failure due to antibodies targeting the ganglionic nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (gAChR). Although the clinical manifestations of AAG have been widely reported, autopsy findings in human cases remain undocumented.MethodsWe examined the clinical course, imaging data, and autopsy findings of a patient with AAG who survived for 14 years.

pmc-13193988.title: Non-chemical, chemical, and biochemical, endocrine disruptors: biphasic health effects and pathophysiological insights
pmc-13193988.creator: Nuriye Nuray Ulusu
pmc-13193988.description: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) interfere with hormone synthesis, signaling, and metabolism, leading to reproductive, metabolic, and neuroendocrine dysfunction. Non-chemical environmental endocrine stressors, including electromagnetic fields, noise, artificial light at night, and thermal stress, can disrupt endocrine homeostasis, alter neuroendocrine and hormonal function, affect signaling pathways, oxidative stress responses, and circadian rhythms.

pmc-13383877.title: Ex vivo partial nephrectomy and renal autotransplantation for an ultra-long ureteral stricture with incidental papillary renal cell carcinoma: A 4-year follow-up case report
pmc-13383877.creator: Wei Shi, Guilin Wang, Junsheng Bao, Li Dong
pmc-13383877.description: We present a 44-year-old male with a 10-cm iatrogenic ureteral stricture and severely impaired renal function. Incomplete preoperative imaging resulted in the unexpected intraoperative discovery of a 2.5-cm papillary renal cell carcinoma. To salvage the organ, we performed an ex vivo partial nephrectomy followed by renal autotransplantation.

pmc-13393483.title: Impact of sex on outcomes in critically ill patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage: a secondary analysis of a French prospective cohort study
pmc-13393483.creator: Sylvain Gourier, Marwan Bouras, Karim Lakhal, Yoann Launey, Karelle Leon, Marc Laffon, Claire Dahyot-Fizelier, Antoine Roquilly, Sigismond Lasocki, Olivier Langeron, Anaïs Caillard
pmc-13393483.description: BackgroundAneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) remains a severe condition with high morbidity and mortality. Evidence on sex-related differences in outcomes and complication profiles is inconsistent. We assessed the association between sex and 90-day functional outcome and ICU complications in aSAH patients requiring intensive care.

pmc-13414858.title: Hybrid Drug Delivery System Designed from Spatiotemporal Hierarchical Controlled-Release Strategy Co-Delivering Rutin and Resveratrol for Coordinated Anti-Tumor Immunotherapy
pmc-13414858.creator: Weinan Li, Sisi Yan, Yingying Gao, Yuhan Fu, Yutong Mei, Yanhong Wang, Zhixin Yang
pmc-13414858.description: Background: The highly heterogeneous and dynamically evolving tumor microenvironment leads to the development of drug resistance and recurrence in traditional therapies. Although immunotherapy demonstrates unique advantages, its clinical utility remains constrained by the suboptimal immunogenicity and the limited effect of monotherapy.

pmc-13634168.title: Inter-anesthesiologist Practice Variation in Vasopressor Administration for Intraoperative Hypotension: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13634168.creator: Denis George, Nicolas Van Rompaey, Emmanuel Noel
pmc-13634168.description: IntroductionIntraoperative hypotension (IOH) is common and has been associated with postoperative organ injury, morbidity, and mortality. Although its incidence and treatment thresholds have been investigated, variation in vasopressor administration across individual anesthesiologists remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to assess inter-anesthesiologist variation in documented vasopressor administration in response to IOH during elective non-cardiac surgery.
